reason: The cited evidence (E1) shows carbide formation occurred in a different RHEA (Al0.3NbTa0.8Ti1.5V0.2Zr) during similar processing, supporting the general feasibility of carbide formation. However, it provides no support for the specific claims about nanoscale dispersion, uniform distribution, dislocation pinning, or the predicted strength-ductility improvement in the NbTaHfTiZr system.
premises: Carbon addition during mechanical alloying of refractory high-entropy alloys can lead to carbide formation.
Carbide precipitates can form during SPS processing even under a protective atmosphere.
Nanoscale carbide precipitates can act as obstacles to dislocation motion and pin dislocations.
Uniformly dispersed nanoscale carbides can improve strength while preserving ductility.
A 0.2 wt% carbon addition will produce uniformly dispersed nanoscale carbides in NbTaHfTiZr.
